description:
Jade Plant (Crassula spp.) is a popular succulent with thick, shiny leaves. It is toxic to cats, even though the exact toxic compound has not been clearly identified.

The plant can irritate the stomach and may also affect the nervous system. Cats may chew jade plants because the leaves are firm and easy to reach on a windowsill or shelf. All parts of the plant should be treated as unsafe.

After eating jade plant, a cat may vomit, have diarrhea, lose interest in food, seem tired, or become unsteady. Keep jade plants out of reach, and contact a veterinarian if your cat eats any amount, especially if symptoms are repeated or your cat seems weak or wobbly.
name: Jade Plant
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: unidentified toxic principle; the plant's fleshy leaves and stems are the primary exposure source
Mechanism: unknown; likely involves direct GI irritation combined with a mild neurological component
Symptoms: vomiting, depression, unsteady gait (ataxia), slow heart rate; symptoms are usually mild
All parts of the plant are toxic — leaves, stems, and roots
Seek veterinary advice if your cat shows signs of unsteadiness or lethargy after contact with the plant

symptoms.name: Vomiting
symptoms.onset: Acute (Clinical signs typically appear shortly after ingestion).
